newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM begins northeast tour amid rebel strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM begins northeast tour amid rebel strike.

text.p: Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral inaugurated a railway line in northeastern India on Monday as separatist guerrillas called a day-long strike to protest against his visit.
Gujral arrived amid heavy security in the capital of Assam state, Guwahati, at the start of a five-day tour of seven states in the hilly region predominantly populated by tribespeople.
"We have very disturbing intelligence feedback that the guerrillas will make their presence felt during the prime minister's tour of the region," a senior security officer told Reuters.

The outlawed United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) called the 12-hour strike in Assam. "It has been called in protest against the fascist Indian government and its representative, the prime minister," ULFA leader Prabin Bora said in a statement.
Formed in 1979, the ULFA is fighting for the independence of the tea- and oil-rich Assam, the biggest state in the region.
Businesses and government offices were mostly closed in Guwahati, residents said. Few civilian vehicles were seen on the roads.
Assam's ruling Asom Gana Parishad, one of 15 parties supporting Gujral's centre-left United Front coalition in New Delhi, appealed to the ULFA to call off the strike.
Some two dozen people were killed over the weekend in insurgency-related violence in the sprawling and remote northeastern region, officials said.
Authorities tightened security ahead of Gujral's first trip to the region. "We have intensified our counter-insurgency operations from Saturday," a senior military official told Reuters in Guwahati.
A separate rebel group in the state of Manipur, the Revolutionary People's Front, called a strike for May 22, when Gujral is scheduled to visit that province.

Last year, Gujral's predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, announced a 61 billion rupee ($1.7 billion) aid package for the northeastern region, which has more than 200 ethnic groups and borders Burma, China, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
